sections.title: 1. Definitions and scope
body: 1.1 "Data Protection Law" means the UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and any other data protection law applying to the parties, as amended.
1.2 "Personal Data", "Controller", "Processor", "Data Subject", "Processing" and "Personal Data Breach" have the meanings given in Data Protection Law.
1.3 "Services" means access to the Revise 360 website, experiences, worksheets and teacher dashboard under the Customer's subscription.

1.4 This agreement applies whenever Revise 360 processes Personal Data on the Customer's behalf. Where the Customer hosts its own copy of the backend, Revise 360 processes no pupil Personal Data and only clauses 9, 11 and 13 apply.
1.5 If this agreement conflicts with any other agreement between the parties, this agreement prevails on data protection matters.

sections.title: 2. Roles
body: 2.1 The Customer is the Controller and determines the purposes and means of processing, including which usernames are used and which pupils may use the Services.
2.2 Revise 360 is the Processor and processes Personal Data only on the Customer's documented instructions.

2.3 The Customer warrants that it has a lawful basis for the processing, has provided the necessary privacy information to pupils and parents, and that the usernames it issues do not contain more Personal Data than necessary.

sections.title: 3. Instructions
body: 3.1 Revise 360 processes Personal Data only: (a) as set out in Annex A; (b) on the Customer's further documented instructions; or (c) where required by law, in which case it will tell the Customer first unless the law forbids it.
3.2 Revise 360 will tell the Customer if, in its opinion, an instruction infringes Data Protection Law.

3.3 Revise 360 will not sell Personal Data, use it for advertising or marketing, use it to train machine learning models, or use it for any purpose of its own. Aggregated, anonymised statistics that cannot identify any Data Subject or Customer may be used to improve the Services.

sections.title: 4. Confidentiality and staff
body: 4.1 Revise 360 ensures that anyone authorised to process Personal Data is bound by a duty of confidentiality and has received appropriate data protection guidance.
4.2 Access is limited to those who need it to provide or support the Services.

sections.title: 5. Security
body: 5.1 Revise 360 implements the technical and organisational measures in Annex B, appropriate to the risk, taking account of the state of the art, the costs of implementation and the nature of the processing.
5.2 The design minimises risk: no names, contact details or credentials are processed, and PINs never leave the device in a readable form.
5.3 Revise 360 may update the measures in Annex B provided the level of protection is not reduced.

sections.title: 6. Sub-processors
body: 6.1 The Customer gives general authorisation for the sub-processors listed in Annex C.

6.2 Revise 360 will give the Customer at least 30 days' notice by email before adding or replacing a sub-processor. The Customer may object on reasonable data protection grounds within that period, and if the parties cannot resolve the objection the Customer may terminate the affected Services without penalty and receive a pro-rata refund.
6.3 Revise 360 imposes on each sub-processor obligations equivalent to those in this agreement and remains fully liable for their performance.

sections.title: 7. International transfers
body: 7.1 Personal Data is stored in the United Kingdom and the European Economic Area.

7.2 Any transfer outside the UK is made under an adequacy decision, the UK International Data Transfer Agreement or Addendum, or another lawful transfer mechanism, and Revise 360 will provide details on request.

sections.title: 8. Assistance to the Customer
body: 8.1 Taking account of the nature of the processing, Revise 360 will assist the Customer by appropriate technical and organisational measures in responding to requests from Data Subjects exercising their rights.
8.2 Where a request is made directly to Revise 360, it will refer the Data Subject to the Customer and tell the Customer promptly.

8.3 Revise 360 will assist the Customer with data protection impact assessments and any prior consultation with the Information Commissioner, and will provide the supporting material described in its data protection policy.

sections.title: 9. Personal data breaches
body: 9.1 Revise 360 will notify the Customer without undue delay, and in any case within 24 hours, of becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting the Customer's Personal Data.

9.2 The notification will describe the nature of the breach, the categories and approximate number of Data Subjects and records affected, the likely consequences, the measures taken or proposed, and a contact point.

9.3 Revise 360 will assist the Customer in meeting its own obligations to the Information Commissioner and to Data Subjects, and will not notify any third party without the Customer's consent unless required by law.

sections.title: 10. Deletion and return
body: 10.1 During the subscription, the Customer may delete any record or export its data at any time from the teacher dashboard.
10.2 Progress records untouched for 12 months are deleted automatically.

10.3 On termination, Revise 360 will delete all of the Customer's Personal Data within 30 days, or return it first if the Customer asks within that period, except where storage is required by law. Written confirmation of deletion is provided on request.

sections.title: 11. Audit
body: 11.1 Revise 360 will make available all information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance with Article 28, and will respond to the Customer's reasonable written questions, including completing a supplier security questionnaire, within 30 days.

11.2 The Customer may audit no more than once a year, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, without unreasonable disruption, and subject to confidentiality. More frequent audits are permitted after a Personal Data Breach or where required by a regulator.

sections.title: 12. Liability
body: 12.1 Each party is liable for its own breaches of Data Protection Law. Liability under this agreement is subject to any limitations in the subscription terms, except that nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited, including for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or fraud.

sections.title: 13. Term, changes and law
body: 13.1 This agreement takes effect when the subscription starts and continues while Revise 360 processes Personal Data for the Customer.
13.2 Material changes will be notified at least 30 days in advance; if the Customer objects it may terminate without penalty.
13.3 This agreement is governed by the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction.

sections.title: Annex B — technical and organisational measures

bullets: Data minimisation by design: no names, email addresses, contact details or dates of birth are collected; PINs are never transmitted or stored in readable form.
Encryption: HTTPS for all traffic; encryption at rest by the hosting platform.
Access control: dashboard access requires a per-school key, compared in a way that resists timing attacks; production access is limited to authorised personnel with multi-factor authentication.
Application security: request size limits, input validation, parameterised database queries, and no execution of user-supplied content.
Separation: each school's dashboard access is scoped by its own key; keys are never shared between schools.
Resilience: managed hosting with platform-level redundancy and backups; work continues offline on the device and syncs when the connection returns.
Retention control: automated weekly deletion of records untouched for 12 months.
Testing: changes are tested before release, including automated checks of the sign-in, sync and dashboard paths.
